audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted their own whys[] line: win[0] said Aurora where the why says level 1 favours you; win[2] and win[3] said Wukong where the whys say her Q poke out-trades you and level 4 'stays hers'; win[5] said Wukong where the why hands her the window. The whys for rows 4 and 5 were also labelled for the wrong stages (row 4 is Level 6, but whys[4] talks about level 5).
audit.why: Aurora out-ranges Wukong from 3 onward — Twofold Hex is 900 range on 9s, The Weirding slows and hops her backward on 15s, and Across the Veil blinks 700 units into invisibility on 22s. Wukong owns level 1 and the two-item side lane. The packet levelChart (Wukong / Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Skill / Aurora / Wukong) matches both the mechanics and the whys indices.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5 flipped in BOTH layers as matched pairs; whys[4] and whys[5] re-pointed at the stages they actually sit on.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the level 6 spike said her W has a recast that escapes your all-in.
audit.why: Across the Veil has no recast — it is a single 22/21/20/19/18s leap. The teleport belongs to Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s), which creates a slowing area she can teleport across. A 140s rank-1 ultimate is the most punishable cooldown in the matchup and the page never gave the number.
audit.corrected: 140s Between Worlds into spikes[1].text, phases[4].why and whys[4]; 22s Across the Veil into phases[2].why and phases[5].why; 9s Twofold Hex and 15s The Weirding into phases[2].why and phases[3].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] said she uses W to 'dodge your E', and the late-game text told you to build armour.
audit.why: Across the Veil makes her invisible on landing — Nimbus Strike is a targeted dash, so it is the invisibility that breaks the target lock, not the movement. And Aurora's damage is magic, so armour is the wrong stat; the same entry already correctly recommends Mercury's Treads.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[1] restated around the target-lock break; armour swapped to magic resist in late.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aurora must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Twofold Hex is 900 range on a 9s cooldown and Across the Veil is a 22s blink into invisibility — she out-ranges and slips you.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twofold Hex's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Still hers: The Weirding slows you and hops her backward on 15s, so your gap-close lands into empty ground. Farm and wait for 6.

edits.before: Cyclone’s double knockup wins every committed brawl. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aurora's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1 — if she spends it to zone you off, your Cyclone wins the brawl she just started.

edits.before: Black Cleaver is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Twofold Hex's cooldown.
edits.after: Her first item outpokes your Black Cleaver — close only when Across the Veil's 22s is spent.

edits.before: Level 5 evens out during her W and escape cooldown windows.
edits.after: Level 6 evens out — Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1.

edits.before: Aurora's level 6 R zone control wins the all-in against your dive.
edits.after: Her first item lets Twofold Hex poke you out before you reach her.

edits.before: Her R Between Worlds zones a huge area and her W recast escapes your all-in, so bait the W dash before you commit Cyclone.
edits.after: Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1 and lets her teleport across its own zone, so bait Across the Veil first, then commit Cyclone.

edits.before: Late game swings back to you because your Cyclone dive and armor let you push through her zone and kill her the moment she can't W away.
edits.after: Late game swings back to you because your Cyclone dive and magic resist let you push through her zone and kill her the moment she can't W away.

edits.before: Use W spirit-dash to dodge your E
edits.after: Across the Veil breaks your E lock

notes: The whys[] array here is written for stages one row off the labels it renders against (whys[4] described 'level 5' on the Level 6 row); I re-pointed rows 4 and 5, but the whole array is worth a look. The 'W recast' in spikes[1] was invented — Across the Veil has no recast, the teleport is on Between Worlds. Mirror notes confirm the three suspectNames on the aurora side were false positives.
